newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Jan-April BOP surplus $317 million.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Jan-April BOP surplus $317 million.

text.p: The Philippine balance of payments surplus narrowed to $317 million in the first four months of the year compared with $1.43 billion in the year-earlier period, the latest data released by the central bank showed on Monday.
The data also showed the current account deficit widened to $2.02 billion during the four-month period versus $1.47 billion last year.
The capital and financial account from January to April made up for the deficit in the current account with a surplus of $2.81 billion compared with last year's $2.88 billion.
The latest data from the central bank does not show yet the impact of the currency turmoil in the region which began to simmer in April.
The central bank had spent almost $2.0 billion of its foreign currency reserves in a futile defence of the peso which was effectively devalued on July 11.
Net inflows from medium and long-term loans of $1.33 billion mostly shored up the capital and financial account in the first four months.
This was followed by a rise in banks' foreign exchange assets of $956 million, net inflow of short-term capital of $369 million and net investments of $166 million.
